subject: BrightGrid billing hold — next steps for refund / VAT evidence
messages:
From: BrightGrid Billing <billing@brightgrid.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: payments on hold and partial refunds — action required

Hi Laura,

We've received multiple failed captures over the last 48 hours and Stripe has placed our account into a temporary "merchant review" hold. Our last invoice with Redwood (BG-9821 / 2027-03-01) shows a partial capture followed by a reversal; our finance team sees a $12,400 debit and a subsequent refund for $6,200. Stripe's notice says they need proof of service and up-to-date VAT registration to clear the hold.

Can you please: 
- Confirm the invoice number you billed against and whether any refunds were issued from your side.
- Provide the signed SOW or delivery confirmation (we can accept a PDF).
- Share Redwood's VAT registration number and a VAT invoice copy for our records.

We're blocked from reconciling this quarter without the documents and Stripe is threatening to delay payouts for another week.

I've attached the invoice and Stripe's hold notice. Happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Clara Mendes
Billing Manager, BrightGrid Inc.
billing@brightgrid.com
attachments: invoice_BG-9821-0327.pdf, stripe_hold_notice.eml

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: billing@brightgrid.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: payments on hold and partial refunds — action required

Hi Clara —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the hold notice. We're sorry for the disruption. Quick summary from our side: 
- Invoice BG-9821 (period 2027-03) was billed on 2027-03-01 for $12,400. We processed a single capture for that invoice; we do not have any automated refunds recorded on our billing system.
- I have asked Payments to pull the raw transaction logs from our Stripe merchant account to verify whether a reversal originated on our end or from the acquirer.

Next steps we will take today: 
1) Ben (cc'd) will pull the Stripe transaction events and attach the capture/auth logs.
2) Marissa (cc'd) on finance will attach our VAT invoice copy and Redwood's EU VAT registration (EU-RED-77729).
3) If it's helpful, we can provide a signed delivery confirmation for the service window (Feb 20–28).

Can you confirm the best contact at Stripe for case escalation? If you prefer, we can loop Stripe and coordinate directly. I'll follow up by EOD with the logs.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: billing@brightgrid.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: payments on hold and partial refunds — action required

Hi Clara / Laura,

Attached are the Stripe event logs and the transaction timeline we pulled. Key items: 
- 2027-03-01T17:03:12Z — charge.succeeded (amount 12400) — charge id ch_3KX...
- 2027-03-02T02:18:40Z — charge.refunded (amount 6200) — refund id rf_7VY... (refund reason: "acquirer reversed")
- No refunds were issued via our merchant dashboard; the refund event appears to have been initiated by the acquirer or a dispute flow.

I've also attached our delivery confirmation signed by the account team and the VAT invoice (invoice_BG-9821-0327.pdf). For clarity, our VAT reg: EU-RED-77729.

Attachments: invoice_BG-9821-0327.pdf (VAT invoice), stripe_event_export_BG-9821.csv, delivery_confirmation_BG-9821.pdf

Given the acquirer-initiated reversal, the path forward is:
- BrightGrid to open a formal dispute case with your acquiring bank and provide the evidence we attached.
- Meanwhile, we can request Stripe to place a hold on future captures until the dispute is resolved to limit further reversals (this is reversible).
- If BrightGrid prefers, we can try to recover funds via our acquirer channels; that'll require an authorization from BrightGrid permitting Redwood to liaise on your behalf with Stripe/acquirer. A short PO/authorization email is sufficient.

If you want me to loop Stripe support directly (support+merchant@stripe.com) and share the event ids, say the word and I'll do it.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: billing@brightgrid.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: support+merchant@stripe.com
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: payments on hold and partial refunds — action required

Laura / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the exports. I've escalated to our acquiring bank and opened a ticket with Stripe (case ref: STR-88112). We've sent them the delivery confirmation and VAT invoice. Stripe's initial response asks the merchant (Redwood) to provide a signed authorization form if Redwood will act on BrightGrid's behalf for recovery attempts.

BrightGrid authorizes Redwood to liaise with Stripe and the acquirer for this specific invoice (BG-9821). Please consider this email the formal authorization. Our procurement team also needs a short statement from Redwood confirming no duplicate refunds were issued and confirming the covered service dates.

I'll keep you posted when Stripe updates the payout timeline. If we don't see progress by Monday, let's schedule a 30-min call.

Appreciate the help —
Clara Mendes
Billing Manager, BrightGrid Inc.
billing@brightgrid.com
attachments: brightgrid_tax_vat_certificate.jpg
